root.title: The image runs as root
root.reason: It declares no USER (or declares root): a flaw in the application gives root control inside the container and makes escaping it easier.
root.remediation: Add an unprivileged user in the Dockerfile (RUN adduser … && USER app) or run it with --user.

env_secret.title: Possible credential in the environment variable {{name}}
env_secret.reason: The image sets {{name}} to a fixed value (redacted): anyone who can pull the image can read it with docker inspect.
env_secret.remediation: Rotate the credential. Don't put it in ENV: pass it at runtime (a Docker/Kubernetes secret or an orchestrator variable) or, if it's only needed at build time, with BuildKit's RUN --mount=type=secret.

build_secret.title: Credential in the build history ({{name}})
build_secret.reason: History step {{step}} contains {{name}} with a value (redacted). ARGs and variables in a RUN are stored in the image and can be read with docker history.
build_secret.remediation: Rotate the credential now. Rebuild using BuildKit secrets (RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npm …) instead of ARG or ENV, and delete the published tags that carry the credential.

build_url_credential.title: Credential in a URL or header in the build history
build_url_credential.reason: History step {{step}} uses a URL with a username and password or an Authorization header with a fixed value (redacted).
build_url_credential.remediation: Rotate the credential and use BuildKit secrets or a .netrc file mounted as a secret during the build.

add_url.title: ADD downloads files from a URL
add_url.reason: Step {{step}} uses ADD with a URL: the content isn't verified and can change between builds.
add_url.remediation: Download with curl and check the SHA-256 (or use ADD --checksum=sha256:… with BuildKit).

ssh.title: The image exposes SSH (22/tcp)
ssh.reason: An SSH server in a container widens the attack surface and often means there are credentials inside the image.
ssh.remediation: Remove the SSH server; to debug, use docker exec or kubectl exec.

no_healthcheck.title: The image defines no HEALTHCHECK
no_healthcheck.reason: Without a HEALTHCHECK, the orchestrator can't detect a hung or degraded process.
no_healthcheck.remediation: Add a HEALTHCHECK to the Dockerfile or define the probe in the orchestrator.

latest.title: The latest tag is being analyzed
latest.reason: latest changes without notice: what you analyze today may not be what you deploy tomorrow.
latest.remediation: Deploy and analyze immutable tags (a version or @sha256:…).

stale.title: The image was built {{months}} months ago
stale.reason: An old image piles up unapplied security patches in its base.
stale.remediation: Rebuild the image regularly (e.g. every week) to pick up the base image's patches.

remediation.app_upgrade: Update {{package}} to {{fixed}} in the packaged application and rebuild the image.
remediation.app_no_fix: There's no fixed version of {{package}}: consider replacing it or mitigating.

limitations.passive: Passive analysis: ZAP only read the responses to ordinary requests. Injections and other attacks weren't tried, so not seeing them here proves nothing.
limitations.unauthenticated: Without signing in: pages behind a login weren't reached.
limitations.spider: The spider stops after {{minutes}} minutes: a large site isn't covered whole, and pages it didn't reach weren't analyzed.
limitations.not_pentest: This is an automated dynamic analysis, not a penetration test.
limitations.headers: Requests carried the domain's saved headers, but the domain has no session check page, so whether they still signed in wasn't verified: pages behind a login may be missing, and this scan marks nothing it found with them fixed. Set a session check page in the domain's headers.
limitations.headers_checked: Requests carried the domain's saved headers, and its session check page answered with them before and after the scan.
limitations.blocked: {{hosts}} turned the scan away (most requests got a refusal such as 401, 403, 406, 418 or 5xx instead of a page, a 404 or a redirect, or were rate-limited with 429): the scan is incomplete and marks nothing fixed. Allow the addresses scans leave from in the WAF or CDN (the new analysis wizard lists them) and scan again.
limitations.session_lost: The session of the saved headers couldn't be confirmed ({{reason}}): the scan is incomplete and marks nothing fixed.
limitations.api: Only the {{count}} GET and HEAD operations of the definition were requested, with example values: POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE operations were left out, and endpoints the definition doesn't list weren't tried.
limitations.wildcards: Hosts matched only by a wildcard weren't resolved, so they weren't analyzed: list a host by name to include it.
limitations.login_one: Signed in as 1 test user, checked before the crawl. Pages it reached show what that account can see, not what other roles can, and a crawl capped in time may still miss some.
limitations.login_other: Signed in as {{count}} test users, each checked before the crawl. Pages reached show what those accounts can see, not what other roles can, and a crawl capped in time may still miss some.
limitations.login_failed_one: Couldn't sign in as {{names}}: what only that account sees wasn't analyzed, so its absence here proves nothing.
limitations.login_failed_other: Couldn't sign in as {{names}}: what only those accounts see wasn't analyzed, so its absence here proves nothing.
limitations.tools_anonymous: Only ZAP signed in as the test users: katana, nuclei, testssl.sh and httpx looked at the site anonymously.
limitations.tool_skipped: {{tool}} didn't run in this scan, so what only it checks wasn't looked at.
limitations.tool_partial: {{tool}} didn't finish: its part of this scan is incomplete, and what it missed isn't marked fixed.
limitations.nuclei: nuclei ran detection templates only (exposed files, misconfigurations, versions, takeovers, TLS): templates that exploit, fuzz, guess passwords or call out-of-band servers were left out.
limitations.tls_capped: testssl.sh checked the first {{max}} hosts of the scope only.
limitations.ajax: The AJAX spider only follows links, in a browser, for {{minutes}} minutes: pages reached only through buttons, forms or typed input weren't opened.

rls.title: Table {{table}} without row level security
rls.reason: The migrations create {{table}} in the public schema and never enable row level security on it ({{path}}). Supabase serves that schema through its API: anyone with the anon key, which ships in the frontend, can read and change every row.
rls.fix: Add `alter table public.{{table}} enable row level security;` in a migration, then a policy for each operation the app needs (for example, rows whose user_id = auth.uid()). Without a policy, nothing gets through.
rls.reason_schema: The migrations create {{table}} in the {{schema}} schema, which this project's API serves, and never enable row level security on it ({{path}}): anyone with the anon key, which ships in the frontend, can read and change every row.
rls.fix_schema: Add `alter table {{schema}}.{{table}} enable row level security;` in a migration, then a policy for each operation the app needs (for example, rows whose user_id = auth.uid()). Without a policy, nothing gets through.

open.title: {{product}} open to anyone
open.reason: `allow {{operations}}` on {{path}} has no condition ({{file}}): anyone, signed in or not, can do it.
open.fix: Require a signed-in user and check that the data is theirs, for example `allow read, write: if request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId;`, and deny everything else.
open.reason_database: `.{{operations}}` on {{path}} is `true` ({{file}}): anyone, signed in or not, can do it there and everywhere below.
open.fix_database: Require a signed-in user and check that the data is theirs, for example `".read": "auth != null && auth.uid === $uid"` under `$uid`, and leave the rest without a rule (denied).

test-mode.title: {{product}} left in test mode
test-mode.reason: `allow {{operations}}` on {{path}} only checks a date ({{file}}): until then anyone can do it, and when it passes the app stops working.
test-mode.fix: Replace the date with real rules: a signed-in user, and only on their own data (`request.auth.uid == userId`).
test-mode.reason_database: `.{{operations}}` on {{path}} only checks a date ({{file}}): until then anyone can do it, and when it passes the app stops working.
test-mode.fix_database: Replace the date with real rules: a signed-in user, and only on their own data (`auth.uid === $uid`).

any-signed-in.title: {{product}}: every signed-in user can reach all the data
any-signed-in.reason: `allow {{operations}}` on {{path}} only checks that someone is signed in ({{file}}): any account, including one created a minute ago, reads and writes every document.
any-signed-in.fix: Match each collection apart and check ownership (`request.auth.uid == resource.data.owner`), instead of one rule for every document.
any-signed-in.reason_database: `.{{operations}}` at the root only checks that someone is signed in ({{file}}): any account, including one created a minute ago, reaches the whole database.
any-signed-in.fix_database: Give each node its own rule and check ownership (`auth.uid === $uid`), instead of one rule at the root for everything.
